## Recent articles

- [Samsung’s Next Phone Could Stretch Instead of Fold, Leak Suggests.](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/news-samsung-rollable-phone-vertical-sliding-display-leak.md): Samsung may be exploring a rollable phone that expands vertically from 16:9 to 21:9. Here’s what the leak suggests about its design and potential challenges.
- [FAA Grounds US Flights Nationwide, Citing ‘Extraordinary’ Safety Concerns](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/news-faa-nationwide-ground-stop-flight-delays-2026.md): FAA grounds flights nationwide, citing extraordinary safety concerns amid air traffic control communications problems. Here’s what travelers need to know.
- [Toshiba Wins UK Contract to Scale Quantum Networks With BT, Colt](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/news-toshiba-uk-quantum-network-contract-bt-colt-emea.md): Toshiba Europe won an Innovate UK contract to build long-distance, multi-user quantum network subsystems, with BT and Colt testing them on real fiber.
- [Samsung and Google Open AI Glasses Preorders: What $395 Gets You](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/news-samsung-google-ai-glasses-preorders.md): Samsung and Google open AI glasses preorders from $395. Explore Gemini features, Warby Parker and Gentle Monster styles, release dates, and phone compatibility.
- [Apple Wants $50 for More AI Usage: How Much Do You Actually Get?](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/news-apple-creator-studio-ai-usage-packs.md): Apple now sells $49.99 AI usage packs for Creator Studio subscribers. Here’s how they work, who qualifies, and why the extra capacity is hard to predict.
- [This Week in Tech: Nvidia’s Shakeup and AI’s Reality Check](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/this-week-in-tech-nvidias-shakeup-and-ais-reality-check.md): See what you missed in Daily Tech Insider from Nov. 9–13.
- [Google, Meta, TikTok Oppose Indonesia’s AI Copyright Bill](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/news-google-meta-tiktok-indonesia-ai-copyright-apac.md): Google, Meta, and TikTok oppose Indonesia’s proposed copyright changes. Here’s what APAC businesses should know about AI content, news links, and liability.
- [Your Smartphone Camera Wastes Light. HoloCoder Wants to Fix That](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/news-metalenz-holocoder-smartphone-camera-technology.md): Metalenz says HoloCoder could deliver up to 2.5 times more light to smartphone camera sensors. Here’s how the technology works and what remains unproven.
- [Oppo A7 Pro Launches in Europe at €429 With 7,400mAh Battery](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/news-oppo-a7-pro-europe-price-specs-battery-emea.md): Oppo A7 Pro arrives in Europe with a 7,400mAh battery, 80W charging, and a €429 launch price. Compare its specs, regional changes, and buying trade-offs.
- [AI Document Summaries: What Gets Missed and What to Check](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/news-ai-document-summaries-missing-content.md): Learn why AI document tools can miss charts, footnotes, exceptions, and revisions—and what IT teams should verify before relying on summaries for decisions.
- [iPhone 18 Pro Max Wins Battery Test Against Google, Motorola, and OnePlus](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/news-iphone-18-pro-max-battery-test-32-smartphones.md): The iPhone 18 Pro Max topped CNET’s 32-phone battery test, but cheaper smartphones delivered surprising results. See which models performed best.
- [Motorola Edge 70 Android 17 Update Reported in UK and Italy as Some Phones Are Still Waiting](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/news-motorola-edge-70-android-17-update-emea-uk-italy.md): Motorola Edge 70 Android 17 updates are reportedly reaching the UK and Italy, but regional delays and user-reported issues leave some owners waiting.
- [RHB Becomes First Malaysian Bank to Combine DuitNow Online and Recurring Payments](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/news-rhb-duitnow-online-recurring-payments-apac.md): RHB becomes Malaysia’s first bank to combine DuitNow online and recurring payments through one gateway. See what changes for merchants and the rollout limits.
- [Google Voice Is Changing How Your Texts Look — With a Bigger Upgrade Still Missing](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/news-google-voice-web-redesign-sms-mms.md): Google Voice’s web redesign brings grouped text bubbles and SMS/MMS labels, while new code discoveries raise questions about future RCS support.
- [ChatGPT Is Retiring Two Voice Modes Dec. 11 — What Happens to Your Chats?](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/news-chatgpt-voice-modes-december-11.md): Two ChatGPT voice modes disappear Dec. 11, but your chats stay. Here’s how GPT-Live takes over and what happens to existing recordings.
- [Motorola Signature 27 vs Pixel 11 Pro XL: 7,000mAh Battery or $300 Savings?](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/news-motorola-signature-27-pixel-11-comparison.md): A 7,000mAh battery, 90W charging and a $300 price gap put Motorola’s Signature 27 against Google’s Pixel 11 Pro XL in a flagship buying decision.
- [AI Search for Ecommerce: 8 Checks to Improve Product Visibility](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/ai-search-for-ecommerce.md): Learn how to optimize AI search for ecommerce in eight steps, from structured data and crawlability to merchant feeds, product citations, and referral tracking.
- [Microsoft Outlook Down: Over 130,000 Outage Reports as Email, Teams Disrupted](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/news-microsoft-outlook-outage-130000-reports-2026.md): Microsoft Outlook outage triggers over 130,000 reports as Microsoft 365 services face disruptions. Here’s what happened and the latest recovery updates.
- [Windows 11 Photos Will Add Adobe AI Tools: What Users Need to Know](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/news-windows-11-photos-adobe-ai-tools.md): Adobe AI tools are coming to Windows 11 Photos. Learn what they’ll do, who gets access first, and what Adobe hasn’t announced yet.
- [Nothing OS 5: 7 Hidden Gems and How to Try Them](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/news-nothing-os-5-best-features-to-try.md): Discover 7 Nothing OS 5 features worth trying, including Glyph controls, new widgets, privacy tools, and multitasking improvements on Nothing phones.
- [Apple Supplier Reports Work on AI Glasses and Smart Earphones](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/news-apple-ai-glasses-smart-earphones-apac-china.md): An Apple supplier reports work on AI glasses and smart earphones. Explore what remains unconfirmed and what IT teams should check before workplace adoption.
- [EU Proposes Crackdown on Subscription Traps, Addictive Apps](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/news-eu-digital-fairness-subscription-traps-emea.md): The EU’s Digital Fairness Act proposal targets subscription traps and addictive app design. Here’s what EU consumers and businesses should prepare for.
- [November PYPL Index: Objective-C Outranks Swift as Python Leads](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/news-pypl-november-2026-objective-c-swift.md): November’s PYPL Index puts Objective-C ahead of Swift as Python leads. Explore what tutorial-search interest means for developer training and migration plans.
- [Apple Support Community to Close Nov. 20 After 28 Years](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/news-apple-support-community-closing.md): Apple Support Community closes Nov. 20 after 28 years. Learn what IT teams should save, which support links to review, and where users can turn for help.
- [Apple Harbor Explained: What We Know So Far](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/news-apple-harbor-local-ai-macs-explained.md): Apple’s Claris is testing Harbor, an app for running local AI across multiple Macs. Here’s what we know about its features, compatibility, and release.

    ;(() => {
        try {
            const match = location.pathname.match(/^\/sites\/([^/]+)\//)
            const scope = match ? match[1] : location.hostname
            const ids = JSON.parse(
                localStorage.getItem("sfl-saved-ids:" + scope) || "[]",
            )
            const prog = JSON.parse(
                localStorage.getItem("reading-progress:" + scope) || "{}",
            )
            const saved = new Set(ids)

            for (const el of document.querySelectorAll("[data-save-toggle]")) {
                const on = saved.has(
                    el.getAttribute("data-save-item-type") +
                        ":" +
                        el.getAttribute("data-save-id"),
                )
                if (on) el.setAttribute("data-saved", "")
                else el.removeAttribute("data-saved")
                el.setAttribute("aria-pressed", on ? "true" : "false")
                const label = el.querySelector("[data-save-label]")
                if (label) label.textContent = on ? "Saved" : "Save for later"
            }

            // The article widget. Both flags live on the card because CSS swaps
            // its halves off them, and that has to happen before hydration.
            // `data-resume` is deliberately narrower than `data-saved`: resume
            // shows only where there is somewhere to go, so it is absent below
            // 5% and again on a finished article, which is how the control
            // retires itself without the item leaving the reader's list.
            for (const card of document.querySelectorAll("[data-save-state]")) {
                const id = card.getAttribute("data-save-id")
                const on = saved.has(
                    card.getAttribute("data-save-item-type") + ":" + id,
                )
                const entry = prog[id]
                const pct = entry ? entry.percent : 0
                const resume = on && pct >= 5 && pct < 90

                if (on) card.setAttribute("data-saved", "")
                else card.removeAttribute("data-saved")
                if (resume) card.setAttribute("data-resume", "")
                else card.removeAttribute("data-resume")
                if (!resume) continue

                const label = card.querySelector("[data-save-resume-pct]")
                if (label) label.textContent = pct + "%"
            }

            document.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent("save:rescan"))
        } catch {
            /* storage unavailable — leave server-rendered defaults */
        }
    })()

(function() {
  var uspTries = 0;

  function makeStub() {
    var TCF_LOCATOR_NAME = '__tcfapiLocator';
    var queue = [];
    var win = window;
    var cmpFrame;

    function addFrame() {
      var doc = win.document;
      var otherCMP = !!(win.frames[TCF_LOCATOR_NAME]);

      if (!otherCMP) {
        if (doc.body) {
          var iframe = doc.createElement('iframe');

          iframe.style.cssText = 'display:none';
          iframe.name = TCF_LOCATOR_NAME;
          doc.body.appendChild(iframe);
        } else {
          setTimeout(addFrame, 5);
        }
      }
      return !otherCMP;
    }

    function tcfAPIHandler() {
      var gdprApplies;
      var args = arguments;

      if (!args.length) {
        return queue;
      } else if (args[0] === 'setGdprApplies') {
        if (
          args.length > 3 &&
          args[2] === 2 &&
          typeof args[3] === 'boolean'
        ) {
          gdprApplies = args[3];

            args[2]('set', true);
          }
        }
      } else if (args[0] === 'ping') {
        var retr = {
          gdprApplies: gdprApplies,
          cmpLoaded: false,
          cmpStatus: 'stub'
        };

        if (typeof args[2] === 'function') {
          args[2](retr);
        }
      } else {
        if(args[0] === 'init' && typeof args[3] === 'object') {
          args[3] = Object.assign(args[3], { tag_version: 'V3' });
        }
        queue.push(args);

    function postMessageEventHandler(event) {
      var msgIsString = typeof event.data === 'string';
      var json = {};

      try {
        if (msgIsString) {

        } else {

            var returnMsg = {

  function makeGppStub() {

              supportedAPIs: SUPPORTED_APIS, // list of supported APIs

        for (var i = 0; i < __gpp.events.length; i++) {
          if (__gpp.events[i].id == par) {
            __gpp.events.splice(i, 1);
            success = true;
            break;

        }
        clb(
          {
            eventName: "listenerRemoved",
            listenerId: par, // Registered ID of the listener
            data: success, // status info
            pingData: {
              gppVersion: "1.1", // must be “Version.Subversion”, current: “1.1”

              cmpDisplayStatus: "hidden", // possible values: hidden, visible, disabled

              supportedAPIs: SUPPORTED_APIS, // list of supported APIs

            });

      var xhttp = new XMLHttpRequest();

        if (this.readyState == 4 && this.status == 200) {

    /**
     * IAB Vendors.

      iab_vendor_ids_arr = [];

        purpose_legitimate_interests = resultToList(

    ;(() => {
        try {
            const match = location.pathname.match(/^\/sites\/([^/]+)\//)
            const scope = match ? match[1] : location.hostname
            const ids = JSON.parse(
                localStorage.getItem("sfl-saved-ids:" + scope) || "[]",
            )
            const prog = JSON.parse(
                localStorage.getItem("reading-progress:" + scope) || "{}",
            )
            const saved = new Set(ids)

            for (const el of document.querySelectorAll("[data-save-toggle]")) {
                const on = saved.has(
                    el.getAttribute("data-save-item-type") +
                        ":" +
                        el.getAttribute("data-save-id"),
                )
                if (on) el.setAttribute("data-saved", "")
                else el.removeAttribute("data-saved")
                el.setAttribute("aria-pressed", on ? "true" : "false")
                const label = el.querySelector("[data-save-label]")
                if (label) label.textContent = on ? "Saved" : "Save for later"
            }

            // The article widget. Both flags live on the card because CSS swaps
            // its halves off them, and that has to happen before hydration.
            // `data-resume` is deliberately narrower than `data-saved`: resume
            // shows only where there is somewhere to go, so it is absent below
            // 5% and again on a finished article, which is how the control
            // retires itself without the item leaving the reader's list.
            for (const card of document.querySelectorAll("[data-save-state]")) {
                const id = card.getAttribute("data-save-id")
                const on = saved.has(
                    card.getAttribute("data-save-item-type") + ":" + id,
                )
                const entry = prog[id]
                const pct = entry ? entry.percent : 0
                const resume = on && pct >= 5 && pct < 90

                if (on) card.setAttribute("data-saved", "")
                else card.removeAttribute("data-saved")
                if (resume) card.setAttribute("data-resume", "")
                else card.removeAttribute("data-resume")
                if (!resume) continue

                const label = card.querySelector("[data-save-resume-pct]")
                if (label) label.textContent = pct + "%"
            }

            document.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent("save:rescan"))
        } catch {
            /* storage unavailable — leave server-rendered defaults */
